default.speaker: The Keeper
default.text: The Hearth used to feed every road at this crossroads. Now the kingdoms quarrel over the prisons, the roads are empty, and I cannot afford another silent week.

default.speaker: Alden
default.text: Nordia calls what waits beyond the Briarway an enemy of the gods. Give me a blade, a meal, and one healing draught. I will bring back enough to settle my tab.

default.speaker: The Keeper
default.text: Then this is a sponsorship, not a farewell. I risk what remains of the Hearth; you return with loot, a mapped road, or knowledge the next soul can use. Come home before courage becomes pride.

default.speaker: The Keeper
default.text: The shutters rattle exactly as they did before the Hearth fell. I remember the empty roads, the siege, and the moment this door opens.

default.speaker: Alden
default.text: Keeper? You look as though you already know me. Nordia calls what waits beyond the Briarway an enemy of the gods. I need a blade, a meal, and one healing draught.

default.speaker: The Keeper
default.text: Your name is Alden. This time I know the crypt is a threshold, Balor is not the only prison failing, and victory on one road will not save the Hearth. Sit down. We begin differently.

default.speaker: Mayor Corvin Rook
default.text: Nordian and Heltic banners have crossed the western road. Both call it a protective occupation. Neither asked the villages being protected.

default.speaker: The Keeper
default.text: The Hearth recognizes no military claim over its guests or expedition records. Move the refugees upstairs and copy every route map before an army decides it owns the ink.

default.speaker: Eamon
default.text: Three prisons surged within the same hour. That is not coincidence. The seals are one system, and every kingdom has been fighting over pieces of a machine already failing beneath them.

default.speaker: Brina
default.text: Then winning one road was never enough. We need every company home, every nation warned, and choices better than the ones that brought us here.

default.speaker: The Keeper
default.text: Open the archive. Favor, claims, and old orders matter less than what the evidence proves. From now on, every expedition prepares for the whole world—not a single victory.

default.speaker: Mayor Corvin Rook
default.text: The crossroads are gone. The remaining civilians are inside, and the outer palisade will not survive another synchronized breach.

default.speaker: The Keeper
default.text: Then this roof becomes the last road. Bar the doors, tend the wounded, and keep the ledger dry. If the Hearth falls, memory must carry what bodies cannot.

default.speaker: The Keeper
default.text: The old covenant named gods as judges, prisoners as enemies, and mortals as fuel for both. This ledger proves every part of that sentence can be questioned.

default.speaker: Eamon
default.text: Then write the amendment where no throne can hide it. The Hearth becomes guarantor, the prisons become treaties, and every bound power receives a name, a hearing, and enforceable limits.

default.speaker: The Keeper
default.text: Let the final entry read: no eternity without witness; no power without obligation; no hero forgotten beneath another god's victory.

default.speaker: Brina
default.text: Six delegations beneath one roof, and not one banner above the Hearth. I did not think they would agree to that much.

default.speaker: The Keeper
default.text: They did not agree because they became friends. They agreed because every road, grave, and surviving witness proves none can hold the prisons alone.

default.speaker: Mayor Corvin Rook
default.text: Then the crossroads becomes neutral ground by treaty—and the Hearth its first public chamber.

default.speaker: The Keeper
default.text: I have kept promises to gods who deny one another's truths. Today they answer under the same rule they demanded of mortals.

default.speaker: The Hearth
default.text: The lamps bend beneath twelve presences. None can enter fully. Each leaves a sign of assent—and a limit the others may enforce.

default.speaker: The Keeper
default.text: A concord is not trust. It is a structure strong enough to survive mistrust. For now, that is enough to keep the world from ending.

default.speaker: The Keeper
default.text: The Archive proves the prisons were never sacred law. They were weapons, revised into history after their makers won.

default.speaker: The Hearth
default.text: Across every route, seals fail open—not as breaches, but as doors. Gods lose the machinery that made their verdicts eternal.

default.speaker: The Keeper
default.text: What comes next will be dangerous and mortal. At last, it will also be ours to answer for.

death.speaker: The Keeper
death.text: Alden will not return. Put his name in the memorial; a death hidden is a lesson wasted. His route, warnings, and witnessed courage are Contribution—and they are why the next company will go farther.

death.speaker: Mayor Corvin Rook
death.text: Then the Hearth closes? The roads will not grow safer because we lower the shutters.

death.speaker: The Keeper
death.text: No. Brina knew Alden in Nordia. Eamon came from Zarabia to argue the prison must be rebound, not merely slain. I will hear them both, prepare them better, and keep this fire lit.

victory.speaker: Alden
victory.text: The guardian is dead, but the thing beyond it was no ordinary beast. The crypt felt built around a door. Nordia will call that proof enough. I do not.

victory.speaker: Mayor Corvin Rook
victory.text: Your haul settles the Hearth's immediate debt. More importantly, travelers are saying this is the one roof willing to prepare anyone who will face those roads.

victory.speaker: The Keeper
victory.text: Then the Hearth stays mine to answer for. Brina comes from Nordia. Eamon comes from Zarabia with a different account of the seals. We will hear both before I risk the next company.

default.speaker: The Keeper
default.text: The crypt was never the prison. It was built around a threshold—and the road beyond it descends into Balor's domain.

default.speaker: {hero_name}
default.text: Then we carry what remains, tend wounds as we walk, and finish the road before we call it a victory.
